title: Western States 100 – official home page
claims: Western States is described as the world's oldest 100-mile trail race.
The Run starts in Olympic Valley, California, near the site of the 1960 Winter Olympics, and ends 100.2 miles later in Auburn, California.
In the decades since its inception in 1974, Western States has become one of the ultimate endurance tests in the world.
The trail climbs more than 18,000 ft and descends nearly 23,000 ft before runners reach the finish at Placer High School in Auburn.
The course traverses the traditional lands of the Nisenan, Washoe and other neighboring Indigenous Peoples.
The Granite Chief Wilderness reroute project will yield over 7 miles of new and rehabilitated trail, with a significant portion hoped to be open in 2026 and the balance in 2028.
The new Granite Chief trail is higher on the ridge than the existing trail.
The 2026 race recap headline states that course records fell in both the women's and men's races.
